subject: Mutual action plan & hosting questions — Scarlet Health
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Rao <amit@scarlethealth.com>, Nina Caldwell <nina@scarlethealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Mutal action plan & hosting questions — Scarlet Health

Thanks again for the call earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have shared expectations. Big picture: Scarlet wants to host PHI-backed inference for triage workflows and is evaluating Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC (on-prem later). Primary constraints called out on the call: HIPAA/BAA requirement, SOC 2 evidence for controls, and audit visibility for data retention and logs.

Key items we discussed (high level):
- Minimum requirement: BAA signed; SOC 2 Type II evidence or comparable attestation to satisfy security team.
- Preferred route: start on Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) to isolate workload and meet throughput SLAs, with a later Private VPC on customer infra if Scarlet needs full network control.
- Questions from your side: encryption in transit/at rest specifics, where audit logs live, and proof of PHI handling separation.

Immediate next steps I propose (owners & target dates):
1) Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II summary + evidence checklist — owner: Jordan — ETA: 48 hours.
2) Scarlet to confirm whether procurement needs an MoU or will run a formal PO process — owner: Nina/Amit — ETA: EOD Wed 9/2.
3) Security deep-dive call (technical) to review vault/KMS, VPC peering, and log retention — owner: Irene (Redwood) + Amit (Scarlet) — target: next week.
4) Mutual Action Plan (MAP) spreadsheet with gating items and owners — Jordan will share a draft after adding security rows.

Attachments I will include: SOC2 Type II summary (high level), a deployment-mode comparison matrix (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with tradeoffs, and a MAP template.

If that alignment looks right, I’ll send the MAP and SOC summary now. If any of the items above are off, tell me what to change.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. Couple of clarifications from our side:
- We must be on a BAA before any PHI is processed. That’s non-negotiable.
- Our security team will accept SOC 2 Type II summary now to start technical conversations, but procurement will require full report + SaaS questionnaires during contract phase.

Two specific asks we discussed on the call:
1) Can Redwood provide an explicit statement on whether KV caches or token logs could contain verbatim PHI (we need to know where to sanitize/enforce PII redaction)?
2) If we start on Dedicated, will we be able to export audit logs to our SIEM (Splunk) via secure syslog or S3 delivery?

I’ll check internally about procurement timelines, but target is to have an internal decision on commitment model by 9/7. Also looping legal when we reach the BAA draft.

—Amit
Amit Rao

amit@scarlethealth.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 01:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutal action plan & hosting questions — Scarlet Health

Thanks Jordan/Amit — I’ll own the security deep-dive. A few notes ahead of the call so we can be efficient:
- SOC2: we will send a SOC 2 Type II summary (controls mapped to common SaaS questionnaire sections). If you need the full report we can coordinate NDAs/secure transfer or provide it via our compliance portal.
- KV cache / token logs: by default Redwood’s runtime keeps a transient KV cache in GPU memory; we do not persist full request bodies to long-term storage unless explicit logging is enabled. For PHI workloads we recommend:
  * Disable verbose request logging (default off for Dedicated/Private).
  * Enable redaction middleware at edge to strip user-specified fields.
  * For additional assurance, Dedicated or Private VPC allows you to control where logs land and to disable any telemetry export.
- Audit logs / SIEM: Dedicated supports secure delivery (S3+KMS or syslog over TLS) and we can set up an S3 bucket export to your Splunk ingestion pipeline. For Private VPC, full export/local retention is in your control.

Pre-call asks: please share the list of endpoints you will send data to (HIPAA scope) and any retention window your compliance team expects. I’m proposing a 45-minute technical call Wed 9/2 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_SOC2_type2_summary.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)]

Attaching the MAP (filled with actions from today’s call) and the SOC2 summary Irene referenced. I also added a deployment-mode decision row that outlines sample perf/cost numbers for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Short notes inline below: 

- Recommended path for Scarlet (based on conversation): start with Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool, private tenancy) — gives you isolation, predictable throughput for triage, and easier SOC2/BAA alignment.
- If Scarlet requires full network isolation and customer-managed KMS, we’ll plan a Private VPC pilot for Q4 with a migration plan in the MAP.
- During the Dedicated pilot we can:
  * Disable request-level logging by default and send only sanitized audit events to your S3-based SIEM.
  * Provide role-based access for your operators to the model endpoints and a read-only audit stream to Scarlet’s Splunk.

Next steps I’ve entered in the MAP (owners/ETA):
- Jordan: provide SOC2 summary & deployment matrix (sent) — done.
- Irene: tech deep-dive Wed 9/2 10:00 AM PT — invite to follow.
- Nina/Amit: confirm procurement path (MoU vs PO) and internal stakeholders — ETA: 9/2 EOD.
- Legal (Scarlet): start BAA draft once procurement path is clear — placeholder in MAP.
